question: m12
q: Is electricity inflation running ahead of overall inflation?

transcript.answer:
**Yes, electricity inflation is running well ahead of overall inflation.** In the latest CPI data (August 2026), electricity prices were **13.2% higher than a year earlier**, against **4.0%** for all groups CPI.

Recent months:

| Period | Electricity (y/y) | All groups CPI (y/y) |
|---|---|---|
| Jan 2026 | 32.2% | 3.8% |
| Feb 2026 | 37.0% | 3.7% |
| Mar 2026 | 25.4% | 4.6% |
| Jun 2026 | 22.4% | 3.8% |
| Jul 2026 | 6.1% | 3.5% |
| Aug 2026 | 13.2% | 4.0% |

The gap has been wide since mid-2025, though it has narrowed. Electricity was falling year-on-year through the first half of 2025, with declines of up to 35.6% in October 2024. Those swings look largely like base effects from one-off government energy rebates, which would explain the sharp rebound from July 2025 and the drop in July 2026. I haven't confirmed the rebate timing from a source, so treat that as my reading of the pattern rather than a verified cause.

The July 2026 reading of 6.1% and the August rebound to 13.2% also show the series is volatile month to month, so the trend is better read over several months than from any single figure.
